# The Bowling Alley is About Market SEGMENTS, not Markets.

*   [Report this article](https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fpulse%2Fbowling-alley-market-segments-markets-jim-milbery&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=PONCHO_ARTICLE&_f=guest-reporting)

[Jim Milbery](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jmilbery) 

### Jim Milbery

Published Aug 21, 2023

[\+ Follow](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=%2Fpulse%2Fbowling-alley-market-segments-markets-jim-milbery&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_publisher-author-card)

Recently, I've been particularly agitated over a spate of inbound emails pitching me services for ParkerGale and our portfolio of companies. These emails always start with a lead sentence in the same format:

> Jim, I am curious\* about what ParkerGale does about "xyz." Our product (or service) "blah-blah-blah" would be an excellent fit for you and your portfolio. We've had great success with other Private Equity firms and their companies, such as Blackstone, KKR, and Thoma Bravo.

Geoffrey Moore's "bowling alley" strategy is a concept from his seminal work, "[Crossing the Chasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossing_the_Chasm?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)," which addresses the challenges of marketing disruptive technologies. The strategy is an analogy to how a bowling ball knocks down pins in an alley. The pins represent different market segments, while the bowling ball represents disruptive technology. In the context of market adoption, not all segments (or pins) will adopt the technology simultaneously. The "bowling alley" strategy suggests targeting one specific niche market segment (or pin) where the product can solve a compelling problem. Once the product becomes dominant and successful in that segment, it can leverage this success to move on to adjacent market segments, knocking them down like a domino effect. While Moore focused on disruptive technologies, it applies equally well to more mature products.

One of the keys to this approach is understanding that buyers within the same segment likely have similar problems. A customer within one segment is a better reference for prospects within that same segment. For example, a manufacturer is a better reference for another manufacturer than it would be for a bank or an insurance company. I have found that this reference idea holds even for mature markets and products, provided that they are in the same market segment. We define market segments by industry AND relative size (at least). And this is precisely why I get annoyed with these inbound marketing pitches.

Eric V. Holtzclaw 9 months ago

](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/ma-surge-me-reflections-after-2026-south-conference-eric-v-holtzclaw-fm1ec)

[

Moving on from a flopped launch

Sara J Loureiro 6 years ago

](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/moving-from-flopped-launch-sara-j-loureiro)

Blackstone, KKR, and Thoma Bravo have north of $100 Billion of assets under management (AUM). ParkerGale has less than $1 Billion of AUM. We are not in the same segment, folks. I don't care what Blackstone, KKR, and Thoma Bravo do because we have as much in common with them as Apple, General Motors, JP Morgan Chase, or the corner grocery store.

This makes their email pitch lazy or stupid. Either way, I am not going to respond.

\*I find the "curious" bit particularly annoying.

results.title: How a Bowling Alley Can Attract and Retain Customers  | US Bowling Corporation

How a Bowling Alley Can Attract and Retain Customers | US Bowling Corporation

[Skip to content](https://usbowling.com/articles/how-a-bowling-alley-can-attract-and-retain-customers/#main)

## How a Bowling Alley Can Attract and Retain Customers

![You are currently viewing How a Bowling Alley Can Attract and Retain Customers](https://b3544304.assetcdn.net/2.0/3544304/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/US-Bowling-9509-scaled.jpg?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

*   Post published: September 6, 2024

Bowling alleys have long been a staple of entertainment for families, friends, and competitive bowlers alike. However, in an era where entertainment options are vast and diverse, bowling alley owners must be innovative in their approach to attract new customers and retain existing ones. Below are some strategies that can help a bowling alley stand out, drive foot traffic, and ensure long-term customer loyalty.

## **Attracting New Customers**

### **1\. Improve Visibility Through Digital Marketing**

In today’s digital world, an effective online presence is essential. A bowling alley should utilize multiple digital channels to reach potential customers:

*   **Website Optimization:** Ensure your website is visually appealing, mobile-friendly, and provides crucial information such as operating hours, pricing, special offers, and online booking.
*   **Social Media Marketing:** Utilize platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok to engage with the community through fun content, promotions, and event announcements.
*   **Google My Business:** Keep your listing updated with accurate information, photos, and customer reviews to improve local search rankings.
*   **Email Campaigns:** Collect email addresses and send out newsletters with exclusive deals, event invitations, and seasonal promotions.

### **2\. Offer Promotions and Discounts**

Discounts and promotions can incentivize new customers to visit:

*   **First-Time Discounts:** Offer a discount to first-time bowlers to encourage trial visits.
*   **Referral Programs:** Give existing customers a discount or free game when they refer a friend.
*   **Happy Hours:** Discounted bowling rates during off-peak hours can attract new visitors looking for budget-friendly entertainment.
*   **Group Discounts:** Special rates for corporate events, birthday parties, and school outings can bring in larger groups.

### **3\. Host Themed Nights and Events**

Themed nights and special events can create excitement and draw in different demographics:

*   **Glow Bowling Nights:** [Use neon lighting, music, and special effects](https://murreybowling.com/products/make-your-profits-glow/) to create a unique experience.
*   **College Nights:** Offer discounts for students and create a fun atmosphere with music and social events.
*   **League Nights:** Host beginner-friendly leagues to attract newcomers to the sport.
*   **Seasonal Events:** Holiday-themed bowling nights (Halloween, Christmas, New Year’s Eve) can bring in families and groups.

### **4\. Partner With Local Businesses and Schools**

Collaborate with businesses and educational institutions to increase exposure:

*   **Sponsor Local Sports Teams:** Offer discounted team outings or sponsorships to connect with local athletes and their families.
*   **Corporate Team-Building Events:** Create special packages for companies looking to host team-building activities.
*   **School Fundraisers:** Partner with schools to host fundraising events, bringing in families and students.

### **5\. Introduce Unique Attractions and Amenities**

[Adding features beyond bowling](https://usbowling.com/family-entertainment-bowling/) can make your venue a go-to destination:

*   **Arcade Games:** A small arcade section can attract kids and teenagers.
*   **VR Experiences:** Virtual reality games can appeal to tech-savvy customers.
*   **Food and Drink Specials:** Invest in a high-quality menu with signature food items and themed drinks.
*   **Live Music and DJs:** Occasional live entertainment can create a lively and inviting atmosphere.

## **Retaining Existing Customers**

### **1\. Implement a Loyalty Program**

A well-structured loyalty program can encourage repeat visits:

*   **Points System:** Customers earn points for every game they play and redeem them for free games, snacks, or merchandise.
*   **Membership Perks:** Offer exclusive benefits for members, such as discounted rates, priority bookings, and special event access.
*   **Birthday Rewards:** Give loyal customers a free game or discount during their birthday month.

### **2\. Provide Exceptional Customer Service**

Outstanding service is key to customer retention:

*   **Friendly Staff:** Train employees to be welcoming, helpful, and proactive.
*   **Cleanliness and Maintenance:** Regularly [clean and maintain bowling lanes](https://usbowling.com/building-a-bowling-alley/), restrooms, and dining areas.
*   **Personalized Experience:** Get to know regular customers and offer them tailored promotions and greetings.

### **3\. Keep the Bowling Alley Updated and Modern**

Keeping up with modern trends can enhance the customer experience:

*   **Updated Equipment:** Invest in high-quality bowling balls, shoes, and [automated scoring systems](https://usbowling.com/automatic-scoring/).
*   **Comfortable Seating Areas:** Provide spacious, comfortable seating for families and groups.
*   **LED Lighting and Sound Systems:** A modern ambiance with vibrant lights and background music can enhance the experience.

### **4\. Organize Tournaments and Leagues**

Competitive events can foster a sense of community and encourage repeat visits:

*   **Beginner and Pro Leagues:** Cater to different skill levels to engage a wide audience.
*   **Prize Tournaments:** Offer cash prizes, trophies, or free game credits to attract participants.
*   **Family and Kids’ Leagues:** Encourage families to participate in fun competitions.

### **5\. Engage With Customers on Social Media**

Stay connected with your audience through interactive social media engagement:

*   **User-Generated Content:** Encourage customers to share their bowling experiences on social media.
*   **Contests and Giveaways:** Run online contests to increase engagement and reward customers.
*   **Customer Spotlights:** Feature loyal customers or high scorers on social media.

### **6\. Gather and Utilize Customer Feedback**

Listening to customer opinions can help you improve and maintain loyalty:

*   **Surveys and Reviews:** Ask customers for feedback through surveys and online reviews.
*   **Act on Complaints:** Address concerns quickly and professionally to maintain customer trust.
*   **Improve Based on Suggestions:** Implement feasible customer suggestions to show you value their input.

## **Conclusion**
